title: Uniform magnetic fields, flux topology and Pauli coupling

items.title: Magnetic quadratic-form data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and let $d\ge1$ be an integer. Work in
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with
$\langle u,v\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^d}u\overline v$, linear in the first
variable, using the quotient and complex-function conventions of the linked
Euclidean $L^2$ definitions. Fix real scalars $m>0$, $\hbar>0$, and $q$.
Let $A=(A_1,\ldots,A_d)\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$ be real and
let $V\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R)$ satisfy
$V\ge-v_0$ almost everywhere for some finite $v_0\ge0$. Put
$\mathscr D=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ and, for $u\in\mathscr D$,
define
$$\Pi_j^A u=-i\hbar\,\partial_j u-qA_j u\qquad (1\le j\le d).$$
For $u,v\in\mathscr D$ define the sesquilinear form
$$q_{A,V}(u,v)=\frac1{2m}\sum_{j=1}^d\langle\Pi_j^A u,\Pi_j^A v\rangle+\int_{\mathbb R^d}V(x)u(x)\overline{v(x)}\,dx,$$
and write $q_{A,V}[u]=q_{A,V}(u,u)$. Each integral is finite: the test
functions and their magnetic derivatives are bounded with compact support,
and $V$ is integrable on compact sets. The form is Hermitian, densely
defined, and bounded below by $-v_0\|u\|_2^2$.

For $\varepsilon_0>0$ define its shifted form norm by
$$\|u\|_{q,v_0,\varepsilon_0}^2=q_{A,V}[u]+(v_0+\varepsilon_0)\|u\|_2^2.$$
The form is **closable** when every sequence $(u_n)\subset\mathscr D$ with
$\|u_n\|_2\to0$ and
$\|u_n-u_m\|_{q,v_0,\varepsilon_0}\to0$ as $n,m\to\infty$ also satisfies
$\|u_n\|_{q,v_0,\varepsilon_0}\to0$. This condition is independent of the
choice of $\varepsilon_0>0$. When it holds, the **closed form closure** is the
completion of $\mathscr D$ in this norm, identified with its $L^2$ limits;
the corresponding closed form is denoted $\overline q_{A,V}$.

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.1.1, magnetic Hamiltonian and gauge conventions
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §§11.3 and 13.1–13.2, Pauli and magnetic Hamiltonian conventions

items.title: Periodic Sobolev domain for a circle
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let
$S^1=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ with angular coordinate $\phi$, and identify
$L^2(S^1;\mathbb C)$ with $L^2((0,2\pi),d\phi;\mathbb C)$; the omitted
endpoint has measure zero. Let $H^2(0,2\pi)$ be the interval Sobolev space whose elements and first two weak derivatives are in $L^2$. For $f\in H^2(0,2\pi)$ use the continuous endpoint representatives of $f$ and $f'$, and denote their traces by $f^*(0),f^*(2\pi)$ and $(f')^*(0),(f')^*(2\pi)$. Define
the periodic second-order domain
$$H^2_{\mathrm{per}}(S^1)=\{f\in H^2(0,2\pi):f^*(0)=f^*(2\pi),\ (f')^*(0)=(f')^*(2\pi)\}.$$
It is the domain used for the periodic realization of the second derivative;
it imposes no boundary at the angular seam beyond periodic matching.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition, Chapter 9, interval Sobolev domains and boundary traces
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.1, particle configuration with a flux tube removed

items.title: Closability of smooth magnetic forms with locally integrable potentials
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $d,m,\hbar,A,V,v_0$ and
$q_{A,V}$ be the magnetic form on the test core, with $m,\hbar>0$,
$A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$, $V\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$
real-valued and $V\ge-v_0$ almost everywhere. Then $q_{A,V}$ is closable on
$C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ in the shifted form norm
$\|u\|_{q,v_0,\varepsilon_0}^2=q_{A,V}[u]+(v_0+\varepsilon_0)\|u\|_2^2$
for every $\varepsilon_0>0$. Its closure is a densely defined closed
Hermitian form bounded below by $-v_0$.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition, §2.3, closed forms and Friedrichs construction
David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.2, constant-field magnetic quadratic expression

items.title: Closed-form diagonalization in Landau gauge
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, $m,\hbar>0$, and real $q,B$
with $qB\ne0$. On
$L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ close the nonnegative form
$$q_B[u]=\frac1{2m}\left(\|-i\hbar\partial_xu\|_2^2+\|(-i\hbar\partial_y-qBx)u\|_2^2\right),\qquad u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C).$$
Put $\omega_c=|qB|/m$,
$E_n=\hbar\omega_c(n+\tfrac12)$, and let $(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the
complete normalized eigenfunctions of the one-dimensional oscillator with
mass $m$, frequency $\omega_c$, and action constant $\hbar$ in its exact
self-adjoint oscillator realization. For
Schwartz $u$ define
$\mathcal F_yu(x,k)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-iky}u(x,y)\,dy$,
and use its unitary $L^2$ extension. Put $x_0(k)=\hbar k/(qB)$ and
$(Uu)(\xi,k)=\mathcal F_yu(\xi+x_0(k),k)$.
Then $U$ is unitary from $L^2(\mathbb R^2_{x,y})$ onto
$L^2(\mathbb R^2_{\xi,k})$. Writing
$$Uu(\xi,k)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty f_n(k)\psi_n(\xi),\qquad f_n\in L^2(\mathbb R_k),$$
the form closure domain and value are exactly
$$D(\overline q_B)=\left\{u:\sum_{n=0}^\infty E_n\|f_n\|_{L^2(k)}^2<\infty\right\},\qquad \overline q_B[u]=\sum_{n=0}^\infty E_n\|f_n\|_{L^2(k)}^2.$$
Thus the form is the diagonal oscillator form with an unrestricted $L^2(k)$
degeneracy factor; it asserts no finite-area state count.

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.2, Landau gauge and oscillator fibers
Aram Harrow, MIT 8.06 Spring 2016 Lecture Notes, Chapter 4, §§3.1–3.2
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.2

items.title: Spectrum and gauge periodicity of a periodic flux operator
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice, and Dependent Choice. Let
$\kappa>0$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. On
$H=L^2(S^1;\mathbb C)=L^2((0,2\pi),d\phi;\mathbb C)$ use the periodic domain
$H^2_{\mathrm{per}}(S^1)$ defined by periodic endpoint traces and define
$$T_\alpha f=\kappa(-i\partial_\phi-\alpha)^2f,\qquad D(T_\alpha)=H^2_{\mathrm{per}}(S^1).$$
Then $T_\alpha$ is self-adjoint and the normalized characters
$e_n(\phi)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{in\phi}$, $n\in\mathbb Z$, form a complete
orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues $\lambda_n=\kappa(n-\alpha)^2$.
Its spectrum is the closed set $\{\lambda_n:n\in\mathbb Z\}$ and its
spectral measures are purely atomic on that set. For every $j\in\mathbb Z$,
multiplication by $e^{ij\phi}$ unitarily intertwines $T_\alpha$ with
$T_{\alpha+j}$. A smooth periodic unit-modulus function $u$ satisfying
$u^{-1}(-i\partial_\phi-\alpha)u=-i\partial_\phi$ exists exactly when
$\alpha\in\mathbb Z$.

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.3.1, particle on a ring around a flux tube
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.1, Aharonov–Bohm flux and phase

items.title: Closed-form diagonalization with free longitudinal motion
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, $m,\hbar>0$, and real $q,B$
with $qB\ne0$. Let
$c=\hbar^2/(2m)$, $\omega_c=|qB|/m$, and
$E_n=\hbar\omega_c(n+\tfrac12)$ for $n\in\mathbb N_0$. On
$L^2(\mathbb R^3_{x,y,z};\mathbb C)$ close the nonnegative form
$$q^{(3)}_B[u]=\frac1{2m}\left(\|-i\hbar\partial_xu\|_2^2+\|(-i\hbar\partial_y-qBx)u\|_2^2+\|-i\hbar\partial_zu\|_2^2\right),\qquad u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C).$$
Use the wave-number Fourier convention
$$\mathcal F_yg(k_y)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int e^{-ik_yy}g(y)\,dy,\qquad \mathcal F_zg(k_z)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int e^{-ik_zz}g(z)\,dz.$$
and set
$$U_3u(\xi,k_y,k_z)=\mathcal F_z\!\left[\mathcal F_yu\!\left(\xi+\frac{\hbar k_y}{qB},k_y,z\right)\right](k_z).$$
Then $U_3$ extends to a unitary map onto
$L^2(\mathbb R^2_{k_y,k_z};\ell^2(\mathbb N_0))$ by expansion in the
complete transverse oscillator basis $\psi_n(\xi)$. If
$$U_3u(\xi,k_y,k_z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty f_n(k_y,k_z)\psi_n(\xi),$$
the form closure domain and value are exactly
$$D(\overline q^{(3)}_B)=\left\{u:\sum_{n=0}^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(E_n+ck_z^2\right)|f_n(k_y,k_z)|^2\,dk_y\,dk_z<\infty\right\},$$
$$\overline q^{(3)}_B[u]=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(E_n+ck_z^2\right)|f_n(k_y,k_z)|^2\,dk_y\,dk_z.$$

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.2, Landau levels with longitudinal momentum
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.2, longitudinal momentum bands
Aram Harrow, MIT 8.06 Spring 2016 Lecture Notes, Chapter 4, §§3.1–3.2

items.title: Unbounded vector potential and effective Pauli model
items.statement:
Use SI units with mass $m>0$ in kilograms, charge $q\in\mathbb R$ in
coulombs, action constant $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, vector-potential
components $A_j$ in tesla-metres, and scalar potential-energy function $V$ in
joules. For each integer $d\ge1$, let $A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$
be real and let $V\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R)$ be bounded
below. Adopt the general-dimensional minimal-coupling assignment whose core
form is
$$q_{A,V}[u]=\frac1{2m}\sum_{j=1}^d\|(-i\hbar\partial_j-qA_j)u\|_2^2+\int_{\mathbb R^d}V|u|^2,\qquad u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C).$$
Use its closed form closure and the unique self-adjoint representing
Hamiltonian. For dimensional form norms use the fixed reference energy
$E_0=1\,\mathrm J$: apply the closed-form representation to
$q_{A,V}/E_0$ and multiply the representing operator by $E_0$.

The magnetic-field notation is dimension-specific. In $d=2$, with coordinates
$(x,y)$ and $A=(A_x,A_y)$, define the scalar perpendicular field
$$B_\perp(x,y)=\partial_xA_y(x,y)-\partial_yA_x(x,y),$$
in teslas. Thus $A=(0,Bx)$ gives $B_\perp=B$ for a constant signed scalar
$B$. In $d=3$, for coordinates $(x,y,z)$ and $A=(A_x,A_y,A_z)$, define the
field vector $\mathbf B:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ in teslas by
$$\mathbf B=(\partial_yA_z-\partial_zA_y,\ \partial_zA_x-\partial_xA_z,\ \partial_xA_y-\partial_yA_x)=\nabla\times A.$$
No magnetic-field object is assigned by this notation in $d=1$.

For an optional spin-half degree of freedom in three dimensions, define
$$\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S_j=\frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_j.$$
For a core spinor $u=(u_1,u_2)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^2)$,
define the spin-independent form
$$q^{(2)}_{A,V}[u]=q_{A,V}[u_1]+q_{A,V}[u_2].$$
For a declared dimensionless real coupling $g$, adopt the effective Pauli core
form
$$q^{\mathrm P}_{A,V,g}[u]=q^{(2)}_{A,V}[u]-\frac{gq}{2m}\int_{\mathbb R^3}u(x)^*(S\cdot\mathbf B(x))u(x)\,dx,$$
where $u^*$ is conjugate transpose and
$(S\cdot\mathbf B)(x)=\sum_{j=1}^3S_jB_j(x)$ for the three-dimensional
field vector just defined.
Include this term only in model instances where the resulting form is
closable and bounded below, and use its closed form closure and representing
Hamiltonian. No universal semiboundedness for arbitrary $A,V,g$ is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §§1.1.1 and 1.5, minimal coupling and spin in a magnetic field
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §§11.2–11.3, spin magnetic moment and Pauli equation
Aram Harrow, MIT 8.06 Spring 2016 Lecture Notes, Chapter 4, §3.1, charged-particle Hamiltonian

items.physical_scope: A nonrelativistic point-particle model with a static smooth external vector potential and locally integrable lower-bounded scalar potential on Euclidean R^d, d >= 1, in SI units. The planar field is the scalar perpendicular component and the three-dimensional field is the curl vector. The optional spin-half Pauli coupling is a three-dimensional effective model term only when its form is closable and semibounded; no measured g-factor or relativistic correction is asserted.

items.title: Exact planar Landau spectrum in the linear gauge
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice, and Dependent Choice, and
the adopted spinless minimal-coupling form model. Let $m>0$ be mass in kilograms,
$q\ne0$ charge in coulombs, $B\ne0$ the constant signed perpendicular
field component in teslas, and $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. Let
$A:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be $A(x,y)=(0,Bx)$ in tesla-metres; then
$B_\perp=\partial_xA_y-\partial_yA_x=B$ is its scalar perpendicular field.
Take wavefunctions in $L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$. Set $V=0$ and define the Hamiltonian by the
closed form of the core expression
$$q_B[u]=\frac1{2m}\left(\|-i\hbar\partial_xu\|_2^2+\|(-i\hbar\partial_y-qBx)u\|_2^2\right),\qquad u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C).$$
The resulting Friedrichs Hamiltonian is unitarily equivalent, under partial
Fourier transformation in $y$ followed by
$x=\xi+\hbar k/(qB)$, to the constant family of oscillators
$$h(k)=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_\xi^2+\frac{(qB\xi)^2}{2m},\qquad k\in\mathbb R,$$
with its form-closed realization. Its spectrum is
$$\left\{\frac{\hbar|qB|}{m}\left(n+\frac12\right):n\in\mathbb N_0\right\}.$$
Every listed eigenvalue has infinite multiplicity, and every spectral measure
is purely atomic on this set; there is no continuous spectral measure. This is
a conditional model deduction, not a claim that a material realizes the
ideal infinite-plane Hamiltonian.

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.2, Landau gauge and Landau levels
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.2, uniform-field Landau levels
Aram Harrow, MIT 8.06 Spring 2016 Lecture Notes, Chapter 4, §3.2, Landau levels

items.physical_scope: Exact spectral prediction of the adopted spinless nonrelativistic point-particle model on the infinite plane, for a constant nonzero perpendicular field in the unbounded linear Landau gauge. It makes no finite-sample degeneracy count, boundary claim, or empirical assertion.

items.title: Aharonov–Bohm ring spectrum and flux periodicity
items.statement:
Adopt the static ring model of a spinless particle of mass $m>0$ kilograms
and charge $q\ne0$ coulombs constrained to a circle of radius $R>0$ metres.
Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, flux $\Phi$ in webers, and energies in joules.
The angular coordinate is $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$; the
single-valued wavefunction belongs to the periodic domain
$H^2_{\mathrm{per}}(S^1)$; the scalar potential is zero; and a static
tangential vector potential $A_\phi=\Phi/(2\pi R)$ has circulation
$\oint A\cdot d\ell=\Phi$, where $\Phi$ is flux in webers. Under the SI
minimal-coupling assignment, the Hamiltonian is
$$H_\Phi=\frac{\hbar^2}{2mR^2}\left(-i\partial_\phi-\alpha\right)^2,\qquad \alpha=\frac{q\Phi}{2\pi\hbar},$$
on that periodic domain. Its energies are
$$E_n(\Phi)=\frac{\hbar^2}{2mR^2}(n-\alpha)^2,\qquad n\in\mathbb Z,$$
with a complete periodic Fourier eigenbasis. For every $j\in\mathbb Z$,
$\Phi\mapsto\Phi+2\pi\hbar j/q$ gives a unitarily equivalent Hamiltonian;
a noninteger $\alpha$ cannot be removed by a single-valued periodic gauge
phase. These are conditional deductions of the ideal ring model.

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.3.1, the flux-threaded ring
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.1, flux and the Aharonov–Bohm phase
Aram Harrow, MIT 8.06 Spring 2016 Lecture Notes, Chapter 4, §3.5, Aharonov–Bohm effect

items.physical_scope: Exact spectrum of an ideal spinless particle constrained to a zero-width circle with static enclosed magnetic flux and periodic wavefunctions. Finite-width rings, interactions, apparatus, and experimental identification are outside scope.

items.title: Pauli square identity and the formal g=2 coupling
items.statement:
Let $m>0$ be mass in kilograms, $q\in\mathbb R$ charge in coulombs,
$\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, and let $A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$
be a real SI vector potential in tesla-metres, with $B=\nabla\times A$ in
teslas. On the two-component
core $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^2)$ define
$\Pi_j=-i\hbar\partial_j-qA_j$. With the
spin-half matrices and $S_j=\hbar\sigma_j/2$ fixed in the effective Pauli
model, the following identity holds on that core:
$$\left(\sum_{j=1}^3\sigma_j\Pi_j\right)^2=\sum_{j=1}^3\Pi_j^2-q\hbar\sum_{j=1}^3\sigma_j B_j.$$
Consequently the quadratic Pauli expression
$\frac1{2m}(\sum_j\sigma_j\Pi_j)^2$ equals the minimally coupled kinetic
expression plus the spin term $-\frac{q}{m}S\cdot B$, which is the formal
effective Pauli coupling at $g=2$. This is a core identity only; it makes no
claim about closed operator domains or the measured magnetic moment of an
electron.

references.title: V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §11.3, Pauli equation and commutator expansion
David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.5.2, spin and Zeeman coupling

items.physical_scope: Formal differential-operator identity on compactly supported two-component spinors for a smooth static SI vector potential in three-dimensional nonrelativistic Pauli-model kinematics. It asserts neither a closed-domain identity nor a measured particle g-factor.

title: Uniform magnetic fields, flux topology and Pauli coupling — Examples

items.title: Longitudinal free motion turns Landau levels into bands
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice, and Dependent Choice. For the
adopted spinless model on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, take mass
$m>0$ kilograms, charge $q\ne0$ coulombs, and the constant field vector
$\mathbf B=(0,0,B)$ teslas with signed component $B\ne0$. Let
$A(x,y,z)=(0,Bx,0)$ in tesla-metres, so $\nabla\times A=\mathbf B$;
take zero scalar potential and free motion along $z$. The closed Hamiltonian has bands
$$E_n+\frac{\hbar^2k_z^2}{2m},\qquad E_n=\frac{\hbar|qB|}{m}\left(n+\frac12\right),\quad n\in\mathbb N_0,$$
where $k_z$ is a wave number in inverse metres and each $E_n$ is an energy
in joules. Its spectrum is the absolutely continuous half-line
$$\left[\frac{\hbar|qB|}{2m},\infty\right).$$

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.2, Landau levels with longitudinal momentum
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.2, longitudinal momentum bands
Aram Harrow, MIT 8.06 Spring 2016 Lecture Notes, Chapter 4, §3.2, free longitudinal degree of freedom

items.physical_scope: The exact absolutely continuous spectrum of the same ideal spinless point-particle model on R^3 with a constant perpendicular field and free motion in the field direction. No finite sample, material, or empirical claim is included.

items.title: Half-flux ground-state crossing on the ring
items.statement:
In the ideal spinless ring model, at dimensionless flux
$\alpha=q\Phi/(2\pi\hbar)=1/2$ the ground energy is twofold degenerate at
the Fourier labels $n=0$ and $n=1$. At $\alpha=0$ the ground state is unique
at $n=0$. The scale $\kappa=\hbar^2/(2mR^2)$ is in joules and $\alpha$ is
dimensionless.

references.title: David Tong, Applications of Quantum Mechanics, §1.3.1, flux-shifted ring spectrum
V. P. Nair, Notes on Quantum Mechanics, §13.1, flux-dependent Aharonov–Bohm phase

items.physical_scope: Exact level comparison in the ideal spinless ring model with periodic wavefunctions. It does not include spin, finite-width effects, disorder, or an experimental measurement.
